source_note: 15 schools verified in signed-in MySchools with only Screened With Assessment and Brooklyn/Manhattan filters selected. Public program facts only; no profile, account URLs or personal estimates. Historical demand labeled “last year” by MySchools; exact measurement year not printed in the inspected panels.

schools.name: NYC iSchool
schools.deadline: School posts Dec 7, 2026, 8pm; submit by Dec 4 if possible
schools.task: Read the school model, FAQs and current course descriptions. The form asks why you want to attend and what excites you (at least one paragraph), plus anything else the school should know. Faculty score understanding of the model, following directions and a distinctive personal response. Draft separately, then paste into the form; the school says you cannot save and return.
schools.caution: The school’s process page still says 2025–26 and 67% DIA; current MySchools says 66%. Its activity page posts a later Dec 7 deadline; the MySchools application remains due Dec 4.

schools.name: Gramercy Arts High School — Capstone Scholars
schools.deadline: No separate current deadline visible; confirm with school
schools.task: Apply to Capstone in MySchools before uploading. Write a one-page essay about a recent event that caught your attention and how you could express your thoughts and feelings through art. Upload the essay and indicate Visual Arts and/or Theater Arts interest. This is the assessed Capstone route; the separate M66A/M66B routes use auditions.
schools.caution: Essay form opened while signed in, but has no visible cycle/date. Confirm it applies to Fall 2027. Questions: Admissions@GramercyHS.org.

schools.name: East Side Community School
schools.task: Complete the shared Consortium essay described above: one response of 500 words or fewer, submitted once through MySchools → Additional Materials. Rank each desired participating program separately.

schools.name: Institute for Collaborative Education (ICE)
schools.task: Complete the shared Consortium essay described above: one response of 500 words or fewer, submitted once through MySchools → Additional Materials. Rank each desired participating program separately.

schools.name: NEST+m
schools.criteria: Average course grades 50%; online admissions activity 50%
schools.task: Write 450–700 words explaining what excites you about joining NEST+m. Use specific examples connecting your values, interests and experiences to its ethos and programs, and explain your contribution to the community. Review the supplied school resources and rubric. Submit the Google Form once; write independently. No entrance test is required.
schools.caution: The prompt file’s title says 2025–26, but its body says 2026–27 and gives the Dec 4, 2026 deadline. School prose describes the grades component as a screened group; MySchools/NYCPS list average course grades. DIA applies only to new/non-continuing seats.

schools.name: School of the Future
schools.task: Complete the shared Consortium essay described above: one response of 500 words or fewer, submitted once through MySchools → Additional Materials. Rank each desired participating program separately.

schools.name: Bard High School Early College — Manhattan
schools.criteria: Average course grades 10%; humanities response 30%; math 30%; interview 30%
schools.task: Register for one 90-minute in-person math and humanities/writing assessment. Math is based on end-of-7th-grade standards; no calculator. Strong assessment results lead to an invitation for a 15–20-minute interview. Take the assessment only once, at any NYC Bard campus; the score can serve both Manhattan and Brooklyn. Rank each campus separately in MySchools. Registration offers accommodation-specific sessions and documentation instructions.
schools.caution: Upcoming published Manhattan GE date: Nov 7 (9am, noon, 3pm). More dates may be added; availability is only confirmed in registration. The school warns that late testing may yield interview results after the application deadline.

schools.name: Beacon High School
schools.task: Register for ONE in-person written-response session. Respond to an on-demand prompt, on one lined sheet (front and back). Published examples concern growth/contribution in a Consortium school or an intellectual risk; the actual prompt will differ. Choose the appropriate session: some are restricted to students needing documented accommodations. The school page provides separate date/time signup links.
schools.caution: This assessment is separate from the common Consortium essay upload. Posted sessions: Nov 4, 7, 8, 10, 14, 15, 21, 23; Dec 1, 2. Check the session description and live capacity.

schools.name: Manhattan / Hunter Science High School
schools.task: Rank M55A in MySchools and complete the school’s supplemental application and applicant-written personal statement. The school’s embedded instructions explicitly cover 2027–28. Both supplemental components are required. Only one application per student.
schools.caution: Form verified as “2027–2028 … incoming 9th Grade ONLY.” Later form pages require personal information; the exact personal-statement prompt/length was not visible without advancing. Read those instructions before drafting.

schools.name: Frank McCourt High School
schools.deadline: No separate deadline visible; confirm with school
schools.task: The school links an online admissions essay. Select three aspects of FMHS that interest you, then explain why in at least 250 words. Options include revision, competency learning, advisory, peer mentors, integrated curriculum, intersession, block scheduling, collaboration and diversity. Read the form’s rubric.
schools.caution: MySchools calls the 80% component “Interview/Online Form”; the currently linked school task is an essay form. No separate interview requirement or cycle-specific essay deadline was visible. The form includes a 10th-grade choice while MySchools lists no 10th-grade seats; confirm if relevant.

schools.name: Medgar Evers College Preparatory School
schools.criteria: Average course grades 40%; math assessment 25%; essay 25%; interview 10%
schools.task: Current MySchools and NYCPS require math, essay and interview components. The school’s grade-9 page describes an ELA/math assessment and parent/student interview, with prior/current report cards. Contact grade-9 admissions for the Fall 2027 assessment date and registration before using an old form: 718-703-5400; 9thGradeAdmissions@mecps.org.
schools.caution: School pages are stale: grade-9 date Dec 13, 2025; linked registration says April 18, 2026. Its format page also lists a conflicting 40/20/20/20 breakdown. Use the current MySchools/NYCPS 40/25/25/10 criteria pending school clarification. No current signup is claimed.

schools.name: Brooklyn College Academy
schools.priorities: 1. Brooklyn students or residents → 2. NYC residents
schools.deadline: Task and current signup not verified
schools.task: MySchools confirms a school-based assessment but does not specify its format in the selection criteria. The official linked school website returned 404 in the signed-in browser. Contact the school for its current assessment instructions, rubric, deadline and registration: 718-853-6184. Do not assume the task is an essay, interview or test.
schools.caution: The linked Google Site is unavailable. Exact task and signup remain unverified. Brooklyn priority is material: the signed-in display reported no offers last year to the small NYC-only priority group; that is historical evidence, not a forecast.

schools.name: STAR Early College High School at Erasmus
schools.criteria: Average course grades 20%; interview 20%; math assessment 30%; ELA assessment 30%
schools.priorities: 1. Continuing 8th graders → 2. Brooklyn students or residents → 3. NYC residents
schools.task: The school posts an entrance exam/interview on Nov 7, 10am–2pm (with open house), and Nov 9, 4–7:30pm. A separate Nov 5, 6–8pm event is an open house only. Venue: 911 Flatbush Avenue. No separate signup link was visible on the announcement; contact 718-564-2540 to confirm registration, attendance instructions and what to bring.
schools.caution: Announcement combines middle- and high-school sessions; confirm the grade-9 process. Brooklyn applicants have priority over other NYC applicants; do not read one application per seat as easy admission for every group.

schools.task: Register for one 90-minute in-person math and humanities/writing assessment. Math is based on end-of-7th-grade standards; no calculator.
